items.followUp: Define mass and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: A force is described as a push or pull that changes or tends to change an object's state of motion or shape.
rubric.description: Defines force as a push or pull that changes or tends to change motion or shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of force.

rubric.why: The SI unit of force is the newton.
rubric.description: States the SI unit of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the newton (N).

modelAnswer: Force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion, or the shape, of a body.
The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

items.followUp: Define the moment arm of a force.

rubric.why: The axis of rotation is the line about which a body rotates.
rubric.description: Identifies the axis as a line about which rotation occurs.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete definition; award 1 mark if the answer identifies a line or axis associated with rotation but is incomplete.

modelAnswer: The axis of rotation is the imaginary line about which a body rotates.

items.followUp: What is the centre of gravity of a uniform circular disc, and how is it located?

rubric.why: The centre of gravity is the point through which the whole weight of a body may be considered to act.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body's weight acts through this point.

rubric.why: For a uniform triangular sheet, the centre of gravity is at the intersection of its medians, one-third of the way from a side along a median.
rubric.description: Locates the centre of gravity of a uniform triangular sheet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the intersection of the medians or an equivalent one-third-from-the-base location.

modelAnswer: The centre of gravity is the point through which the whole weight of a body may be considered to act.
The centre of gravity of a uniform triangular sheet is at the intersection of its medians, one-third of the way from a side along a median.

items.followUp: Define work and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Power is the rate of doing work, or work done per unit time.
rubric.description: Defines power as the rate of doing work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of power is the watt.
rubric.description: States the SI unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the watt (W).

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work, or the work done per unit time.
The SI unit of power is the watt (W).

items.followUp: Define chemical energy and gravitational potential energy.

rubric.why: Geothermal energy is heat energy obtained from the Earth's interior.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as heat or thermal energy from inside the Earth.

rubric.why: Elastic potential energy is stored when an elastic object is stretched, compressed or otherwise deformed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking stored energy to stretching, compression or deformation of an elastic object.

modelAnswer: Geothermal energy is heat energy obtained from the interior of the Earth.
Elastic potential energy is the energy stored in an elastic object when it is stretched, compressed or otherwise deformed.

items.followUp: State the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the direction of the force.

rubric.why: One joule is the work done when a force of one newton moves an object one metre in the direction of the force.
rubric.description: States the force and displacement in the definition of one joule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying 1 N and 1 m in the direction of the force.

rubric.why: This amount of work is one joule.
rubric.description: Identifies the amount of work as one joule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the work done is 1 J.

modelAnswer: One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object through 1 m in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: Write two features of the kinetic molecular model of matter.

rubric.why: The model states that matter is made up of tiny particles.
rubric.description: States that matter consists of tiny particles.

rubric.why: The particles are in continuous motion, often described as random motion.
rubric.description: States that the particles are in continuous or random motion.

modelAnswer: Matter is made up of tiny particles.
The particles are in continuous random motion.

items.followUp: A student walks 3 m east and then 4 m west. Find the distance travelled and the displacement.

rubric.why: Distance is a scalar quantity; it has magnitude only.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying distance as a scalar quantity.

rubric.why: Distance is the total length of the actual path travelled.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing distance as the total path length.

rubric.why: Displacement is a vector quantity and includes direction.
rubric.description: Explains that displacement is a directed quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying displacement as a vector or stating that it has direction.

rubric.why: Displacement is the directed shortest straight-line change from the initial to the final position; its magnitude is no greater than the distance.
rubric.description: Explains displacement as the directed straight-line change between endpoints.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this explanation, including the initial and final positions.

modelAnswer: Distance is the total length of the actual path travelled; it is a scalar quantity and has magnitude only.
Displacement is the shortest straight-line change from the initial position to the final position, with direction; it is a vector quantity.
The magnitude of displacement is always less than or equal to the distance travelled.
For example, if a body returns to its starting point, its distance is not zero but its displacement is zero.
